I need to find a maximal triangle-free graph on 12 vertices. A maximal triangle-free graph is one where adding any new edge would create a triangle.

The classic construction for maximal triangle-free graphs is the complete bipartite graph K_{n/2, n/2}, which is triangle-free and maximal (adding any edge within a partition creates a triangle... wait, actually within a partition there are no edges, and adding one between two vertices in the same partition - those two vertices have no common neighbors in the other partition necessarily).

Actually, K_{6,6} (complete bipartite graph with parts of size 6) is triangle-free (bipartite graphs are triangle-free) and it's maximal because: if we add an edge between two vertices u, v in the same partition, since every vertex in the other partition is connected to both u and v, we get a triangle u-w-v for any w in the other partition.

So K_{6,6} with parts {0,1,2,3,4,5} and {6,7,8,9,10,11} works perfectly.

The edges are all (i,j) where i ∈ {0,...,5} and j ∈ {6,...,11}.
